correctness.rationale: For 2^a p^b, the Carmichael divisor weights split into a complete power-of-two base block and positive-p blocks whose normalized weights are initial 1's followed by powers of 2. The smallest weight in block j fits exactly under the stated inequality, and failure leaves the next integer after the preceding total unrepresentable. The counting corollary follows by adjoining primes to a suitable power of two. A direct finite verifier checked 3050 triples and 610 b=1 threshold cases with zero mismatches.

originality.rationale: Schwab and Thompson define lambda-star-practical numbers, prove an X/log X upper bound, and explicitly report no reasonable lower bound; their general adjunction theorem is for multiplicative functions and does not directly cover Carmichael lambda. OEIS A336508 and searches under exact and synonymous terminology did not locate the 2^a p^b classification, the b=1 threshold, or the square-root-order lower bound. The current SCOPE archive also had no overlap. Originality remains to the best of our knowledge.

value.rationale: The result completely classifies a natural infinite two-prime-support family for the Carmichael subset-sum notion and converts the simple b=1 criterion into a polynomial lower bound F_{lambda*}(X) >= (1-o(1))*sqrt(X)/log X for a counting problem whose foundational treatment reported no reasonable lower bound.
